Provider brand marks (ImageVector subset)
=========================================

Vendored asset: the path data in `../src/main/kotlin/com/taffygo/browser/ui/core/ui/ProviderMark.kt`
                (fifteen marks on the source's 24-unit viewport. Most sources
                are one path; Cerebras is two and Together is three, and each is
                carried as the source wrote it. The path data is monochrome and
                every mark draws in a tint the caller chooses)
Owners:         Anthropic PBC, Google LLC, OpenRouter, Inc., Moonshot AI,
                OpenAI, Inc., xAI Corp., GitHub, Inc.,
                DeepSeek, MiniMax, Groq, Inc., Together
                Computer, Inc., Baseten Labs, Inc., Cerebras Systems Inc.,
                Fireworks AI, Inc.
Licence:        None, and none is implied by carrying the file. Each mark is
                its owner's trademark. The Simple Icons distribution is
                CC0-1.0, which covers the SVG files and cannot and does not
                license anybody's trademark. The marks fetched from
                lobe-icons v5.16.0 sit under that project's MIT licence for
                the SVG files, and the same trademark limit: MIT covers the
                file, not the mark. Eight marks came from Simple Icons and
                seven from lobe-icons; the split is per mark and is recorded in
                the table below, because it is the file's licence that differs
                and not the trademark position, which is identical for all
                fifteen.
Permitted use:  One group, and one use. This file used to state two: two
                further marks were permitted as the icons of account sign-in
                buttons on screen SCR-701, and they left this file when that
                screen was deleted (decision 0201). A permitted use is not a
                licence — a mark whose one permitted use no longer exists in
                the product has no standing to stay in the tree, so it went
                rather than waiting for a use to be found for it. The
                Cloudflare mark left the same way on 2026-09-20, and for the
                same reason stated the other way round: its row left the
                catalog (decision 0214), so the use it was permitted for
                stopped existing.

                Model providers — Anthropic, Baseten, Cerebras,
                DeepSeek, Fireworks, GitHubCopilot, GoogleGemini, Groq, Kimi,
                MiniMax, MoonshotAi, OpenAi, OpenRouter, Together, Xai. Each
                mark may be shown only as the identifying mark of that vendor's
                own row on screen SCR-404 or on that same vendor's own pages
                SCR-415 to SCR-417, beside the vendor's own name, in a build
                where that vendor is a real provider a person can send a request
                to. Every mark here now names the vendor of its own row. Two
                rows once drew another name's mark: the Gemini mark identified
                the Google Antigravity subscription row until decision 0134
                withdrew it, and the Cloudflare mark identified the Cloudflare
                Workers AI row — that company's own product, with no separate
                mark at either source — until decision 0214 withdrew that one.
                The Gemini mark stayed because it has a row of its own; the
                Cloudflare mark did not, because it had none.

                The three per-provider screens were added on 2026-08-29 and
                widen the permission rather than stretch it. A page that exists
                to set up one vendor is a stronger case than a row in a list is:
                the whole screen is about that vendor, under that vendor's own
                name, and there is nothing else on it the mark could be read as
                endorsing. What the permission still does not cover is a mark
                used decoratively, a mark on a screen about the product rather
                than about that vendor, and a mark for a vendor whose row is not
                really there.

                What the argument rests on, per owner, and it is not the same
                document in every case. Four owners publish brand or trademark
                guidance that speaks to this use directly: Google, OpenAI, xAI
                and GitHub. Moonshot AI publishes a branding guide,
                which is what Simple Icons records as the source of the Kimi
                mark. The remaining owners — Anthropic, OpenRouter, DeepSeek,
                MiniMax, Groq, Together, Baseten, Cerebras, Fireworks —
                publish terms of use and no brand document that was found, so
                for those the argument is referential and nothing more: the mark
                names the vendor whose own service a person is choosing to
                connect their own account to, beside that vendor's own name, and
                implies no endorsement, sponsorship or affiliation. The
                distinction is written down rather than smoothed over, because
                "the owner's toolkit permits this" and "no owner document was
                read" are two different claims and the second must not be filed
                under the first. The removal trigger below is what makes the
                weaker case safe to hold.

                GitHub owns two marks at the upstream source and only one is
                here. The Copilot mark is the GitHub Copilot provider row's;
                the Invertocat was the sign-in button's, and it left with that
                button. They were always two entries under two permissions
                rather than one owner's entry drawn twice, which is why
                removing one left the other untouched.
Removal trigger: A mark leaves this file the moment its vendor leaves the
                launch provider set of decision 0029, the moment its owner
                asks, or the moment the mark is used anywhere other than that
                vendor's own row. That trigger has fired twice, and on two
                different clauses of it. The two account marks went when their
                one screen was deleted (decision 0201); the Cloudflare mark
                went on the first clause, when its vendor left the launch set
                (decision 0214). This is what it looks like when it fires.

                Google          https://about.google/brand-resource-center/
                OpenRouter      https://openrouter.ai/terms

                OpenAI          https://openai.com/brand/
                xAI             https://x.ai/legal/brand-guidelines

Upstream:       https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/simple-icons@16.28.0/icons/<name>.svg
                (eight marks). The other seven are absent from that pin; they
                were fetched from lobe-icons v5.16.0, which still publishes
                them, at
                https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lobehub/lobe-icons@v5.16.0/packages/static-svg/icons/<name>.svg
Upstream repo:  https://github.com/simple-icons/simple-icons
                https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-icons  (OpenAi, Xai, Groq,
                Together, Baseten, Cerebras, Fireworks)
Fetched:        2026-08-19  Anthropic, GoogleGemini, OpenRouter, MoonshotAi
                2026-08-23  OpenAi, Xai
                2026-08-30  DeepSeek, GitHubCopilot, Kimi, MiniMax,
                            Groq, Together, Baseten, Cerebras, Fireworks

The GitHub terms URL added on 2026-08-20 is the live one rather than the one
Simple Icons records: `https://github.com/logos` now redirects to the GitHub
brand toolkit. A provenance record that names a URL which only redirects is one
rebase away from naming nothing. Sixteen URLs were requested again on
2026-08-30 — the fourteen above, Cloudflare's, which went with that row on
2026-09-20, and Meta's, which was in this file then and went with the Facebook
mark. That count is left as it was measured rather than restated each time the
list shrinks: it is a record of work that was done, and the work covered
sixteen. Fourteen of the sixteen answered 200 after redirects. Two — OpenAI's
brand page and xAI's brand guidelines — answered 403 to a plain command-line
client, which is a refusal to serve that client and not
a missing page; they are left as recorded rather than replaced, because a 403
says the resource is there and a 404 would not. Neither was re-read on
2026-08-30, so nothing in this file claims to quote them as of that date.

`GoogleGemini` is Google's Gemini mark and is shown on the `google-ai-studio`
row, because the key Google AI Studio issues is the key that reaches the Gemini
API. It is the mark for that model family, not a mark for the console; if that
reading is wrong the removal trigger above covers it. `Cloudflare` was read the
same way for `cloudflare-workers-ai` — the mark of the company whose product
that row was, there being no mark for Workers AI itself — and that reading is
the reason it could not survive the row: a mark held on somebody else's
product's behalf has nothing left to identify once the product's row is gone.

The five lobe-icons files fetched on 2026-08-30 set `fill-rule="evenodd"` on the
SVG root; the Kotlin transcription keeps that fill type for all five, exactly as
the 2026-08-23 pair already did. The Simple Icons files set no fill rule and are
transcribed non-zero, which is what that distributor authors for.

Two sources are not one path. `cerebras.svg` carries the concentric arcs and the
"C" inside them separately, and `together.svg` carries three petals. Both are
transcribed path by path rather than concatenated into one string: under either
fill rule the union of two outlines is not reliably what the source painted, and
merging them would be a re-drawing decision, which decision 0030 does not permit.
`ProviderMarkTest` asserts the path count of every mark for that reason.

The vendor that is deliberately not here
----------------------------------------

**Z.AI has no mark in this file and its row draws a monogram.** lobe-icons
v5.16.0 does publish `zai.svg`, so the URL-and-checksum half of decision 0030
was available and is not the reason. The reason is the other half: on 2026-08-30
no owner-published document could be found to argue a permitted use from.
`https://z.ai/` and `https://docs.z.ai/` answer, and the catalog's own
`docs_url` for the row resolves, but those are product pages rather than
anything that speaks to the mark; `z.ai/terms`, `z.ai/terms-of-service`,
`z.ai/terms-of-use`, `z.ai/service-agreement` and `z.ai/legal` were each
requested and each answered 404. Every other owner in this file could produce
at least a terms page, and the argument recorded above depends on that.

So the row falls to the product's own monogram treatment, which is legible in
both themes and claims nothing. That is a correct outcome rather than a gap: the
bar decision 0030 sets is only worth setting if something is occasionally on the
wrong side of it, and this is the entry that shows it bites. A Z.AI brand or
terms page appearing later is enough to revisit this; nothing else is needed,
because the file and its checksum are already published.

The model marks' own colours, and the three that are not drawn
--------------------------------------------------------------

Added 2026-08-23, when the provider rows stopped tinting every mark with the
product's own ink and started drawing each vendor's published colour; extended
2026-08-30 with the marks fetched that day, and corrected later the same day
when the lobe-icons colour files were finally requested rather than assumed
about. The values live in
`../../../feature/providers/src/main/kotlin/com/taffygo/browser/ui/feature/providers/ProviderMarkStyle.kt`,
outside `TaffyTheme.colors` because a vendor's brand value is part of somebody
else's mark and a value like that inside the palette invites a later reader to
reuse it as a product token. (That path said `feature/settings/...` until
2026-08-30 and was simply wrong; the file has always been in
`feature/providers`.) That Kotlin file is not checksummed by
`tools/lib/vendored_assets.py`: the register reads one `sha256` fact per
provenance file and this one already spends it on `ProviderMark.kt`. The gap is
small — colour literals and no path data — and it is written down here rather
than left for someone to discover.

**No value below was read from a page the owner publishes as text.** Nor do they
all come from one place, which the sentence this paragraph replaced got wrong:
it said every value below was a Simple Icons `hex` field, and two entries then
contradicted it two lines later by saying they were not. There are three classes
and each entry says which one it is.

  1. A distributor's recorded `hex` field, read out of Simple Icons'
     `data/simple-icons.json` at the pin the path data came from, on 2026-08-23
     and 2026-08-30. Simple Icons also records a `source` URL per icon, which is
     where it says it took the mark from; that URL is reproduced below because
     it is a different claim from "the owner published this number", and
     conflating the two is a mistake this file has made before and each entry
     below is worded to avoid repeating.
  2. A `fill` attribute read out of the `-color.svg` sibling lobe-icons
     publishes beside the monochrome file, at the same pin, on 2026-08-30. That
     is the same kind of claim as the first — a distributor saying what colour
     it holds this mark to be — stated in a file rather than in a metadata
     field. Each such entry records the file's own checksum, and whether its
     paths are byte-identical to the ones transcribed into `ProviderMark.kt`,
     because a colour attaches to path data or to nothing.
  3. No distributor value at all. Two entries are in this class, OpenAI and xAI:
     Simple Icons 16.28.0 carries no icon under either title — checked against
     `data/simple-icons.json` on 2026-08-30, 3453 icons, neither slug present —
     and their lobe-icons files are `currentColor`. Their ink is a reading of
     the owner's own stated rule rather than a number anybody published, and
     each says so on its own line.

  #191919   Anthropic.      slug `anthropic`
            Simple Icons' source: https://www.anthropic.com
  #000000   Moonshot AI.    slug `moonshotai`
            Simple Icons' source: https://www.moonshot.cn — note that this is
            a different host from the terms URL recorded at the top of this
            file, which is www.moonshot.ai. Neither was reconciled against the
            other and neither is asserted to supersede it.
  #8E75B2   Google Gemini.  slug `googlegemini`
            Simple Icons' source: https://gemini.google.com
  #000000   OpenAI.         slug `openai` (lobe-icons v5.16.0)  — class 3.
            `openai.svg` is `currentColor`, `openai-color.svg` does not exist
            at the pin, and Simple Icons carries no OpenAI icon. OpenAI's brand
            page specifies black or white at highest contrast; black is the
            ink, on the same white chip Anthropic uses. That is a rule this
            file read and applied, not a value a distributor recorded.
  #000000   xAI.            slug `xai` (lobe-icons v5.16.0)  — class 3.
            The same, checked the same way: `xai.svg` is `currentColor`, there
            is no `xai-color.svg` at the pin, and Simple Icons carries no xAI

  #5786FE   DeepSeek.       slug `deepseek`

            light ground, which is the ground the chip gives it.

  #E73562   MiniMax.        slug `minimax`
            Simple Icons' source: a file in MiniMax's own GitHub repository,

            `cerebras-color.svg`, requested 2026-08-30, HTTP 200,
            sha256 355c2225284cd06c9cf4246110b60cb21bc86039872981e1be6bb82deec2ffa7.
            Two paths, byte-identical to `PATH_CEREBRAS_RINGS` and
            `PATH_CEREBRAS_LETTER`. The rings carry this fill; the letter
            carries no `fill` of its own and inherits the root's
            `currentColor`, so what the source specifies for the letter is
            "whatever colour the mark is being drawn in". The single-tint
            treatment draws both paths in this hue, which is what the source
            itself paints when the current colour is this hue — an
            instantiation of what the file says, not a re-drawing of it.
  #5019C5   Fireworks AI.   slug `fireworks` (lobe-icons v5.16.0)  — class 2.
            `fireworks-color.svg`, requested 2026-08-30, HTTP 200,

            Three paths, byte-identical to `PATH_TOGETHER_ONE`, `PATH_TOGETHER_TWO`

Groq and Baseten are the only two marks here with **no recorded colour at all**,
and the claim is bounded by what was actually requested rather than assumed. On
2026-08-30 the `-color.svg` sibling of each answered **404** at the pin above
(`Couldn't find the requested file … in lobehub/lobe-icons`), and `groq.svg` and
`baseten.svg` themselves set `fill="currentColor"` on the SVG root and carry no
hex anywhere in the file. Nothing was read for those two, so nothing is
recorded for them: a colour this repository has not read is not a colour it may
publish on someone's behalf. Both marks draw in the product's own ink on the
product's own ground.

Until 2026-08-30 this paragraph said the same of Cerebras, Fireworks and
Together, and of those three it was false. All three publish a `-color.svg` at
the same pin; each answered 200; each carries fills on paths byte-identical to
the ones already transcribed into `ProviderMark.kt`. The sentence had never been
checked against the URL it was making a claim about, and it was the strong form
of the mistake this file exists to prevent — "no value was ever published" filed
where "no value was ever requested" was the truth. Two of the three now draw
their vendor's own colour, so those two marks had been drawn more dully than the
evidence supported; the third is recorded and rejected below, which is the same
outcome it had before but for a reason that can now be read.

The rule is measured, and it is a threshold rather than a list
--------------------------------------------------------------

Contrast is measured rather than judged, because several of these sit at one end
of the range. WCAG 2.x contrast ratios against the badge's own ground in each
theme, and against white; 3:1 is the floor for a meaningful graphical object
under SC 1.4.11:

  Mark            hex       on light #F1EBE1   on dark #1C1B19   on white
  Anthropic       #191919   14.83:1            1.02:1            17.58:1
  Moonshot AI     #000000   17.71:1            1.22:1            21.00:1
  OpenAI          #000000   17.71:1            1.22:1            21.00:1
  xAI             #000000   17.71:1            1.22:1            21.00:1
  GitHub Copilot  #000000   17.71:1            1.22:1            21.00:1
  Kimi            #000000   17.71:1            1.22:1            21.00:1
  Fireworks AI    #5019C5   7.75:1             1.87:1            9.18:1
  Google Gemini   #8E75B2   3.32:1             4.37:1            3.93:1
  MiniMax         #E73562   3.48:1             4.17:1            4.13:1
  Cerebras        #F15A29   2.84:1             5.11:1            3.37:1
  DeepSeek        #5786FE   2.84:1             5.12:1            3.36:1
  OpenRouter      #94A3B8   2.16:1             6.71:1            2.56:1
  Together AI     #EF2CC1   3.05:1             4.75:1            3.62:1
   one per petal  #CAAEF5   1.63:1             8.92:1            1.93:1
   of three       #FC4C02   2.87:1             5.06:1            3.40:1

The near-blacks are invisible on the dark theme: 1.02:1 is not a low ratio, it
is the mark and its ground being the same colour. Every mark that keeps a vendor
colour therefore sits on a white chip of the badge's own size, in both themes,
which is also the ground each of those brands specifies for its dark mark. One
treatment for all of them, rather than a different answer per vendor.

That fixes the dark half and opens the light half, which is the failure this
section was extended to close: a pale vendor colour on a white chip is white on
white, the same disappearance wearing the other theme. So `ProviderMarkStyle`
measures each recorded hue against the chip and refuses the ones that fall
short, and it is a **threshold and not a denylist** — a vendor added later whose
colour happens to be near-white is caught by the same arithmetic that catches
one whose colour is near-black, with nobody having to notice.

Two of the thirteen recorded entries are not drawn, and not for the same
reason.

One fails the threshold outright, on the light side. OpenRouter's slate measures
2.56:1 on the chip, and there is no ground on which it is legible at this size —
it is worse still on the light theme, at 2.16:1. Darkening it would be
publishing a brand colour its owner has not, which is the same act decision 0030
forbids for a mark.

Cloudflare's orange was the second until 2026-09-20, measuring 2.65:1 on the
chip and 2.24:1 on the light theme. It is not listed above any more, because a
hue recorded and rejected is still a fact about a mark this file may draw, and
decision 0214 took the mark. The numbers are left in this paragraph rather than
deleted outright: they say the value was read and measured, which is what the
record is for.

Together AI fails for a different reason, and it is worth being exact about
which. Its entry is three fills and not one, and the treatment here is a single
tint over the whole mark, so "Together's colour" would have to be one petal's
fill painted over all three petals — a re-drawing decision, which is the thing
decision 0030 does not permit and the reason `together.svg`'s three paths were
transcribed separately in the first place. The threshold would not save the mark
either way: the pale petal `#CAAEF5` measures 1.93:1 on the chip, so a third of
the mark would disappear even if the arrangement could be carried. Two of its
three fills do clear the floor on their own — 3.62:1 and 3.40:1 — which is
recorded here because it is the fact that makes the rejection a judgement rather
than an arithmetic result.

Both marks keep the product's own neutral ink on the product's own ground
instead: legible in both themes, and claiming nothing. Their hexes stay recorded
above so that the next person can see the values were read and rejected rather
than never looked up.

The Gemini mark took the same treatment as well, on 2026-08-30, when it was
violet on a chip in the `google-ai-studio` row and product ink on the sunken
ground in the subscription row directly beneath it — one mark drawn two ways in
one list, which was a defect and not a decision. That second row has since
been withdrawn (decision 0134).

Conversion command
------------------

The `d` attribute of each source file, copied with no hand-editing, then
wrapped in the `ImageVector.Builder` call `ProviderMark.mark` makes:

  curl -sS https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/simple-icons@16.28.0/icons/<name>.svg -o <name>.svg
  sha256sum <name>.svg
  python3 -c "import re,sys;print(re.search(r' d=\"([^\"]+)\"',open(sys.argv[1]).read()).group(1))" <name>.svg

A source with more than one path needs `re.findall` rather than `re.search`, and
each result becomes its own argument to `mark`.

The `sha256=` line above is the checksum of the committed Kotlin file, so it
proves the transcription has not drifted since it was recorded. The per-mark
checksums are the upstream proof: they say what was fetched. Both are needed,
and decision 0030 is why — a committed checksum alone is what
`feature/onboarding/vendor/google-identity.txt` has, and that file has to
explain at length that it cannot say where its bytes came from (OD-086).

The 2026-08-20 fetch re-ran the command above against `anthropic.svg` at the
same pin before recording anything new, and got the checksum already on the
Anthropic line. The two new numbers were therefore produced by a method that
reproduces a number this repository had already accepted, rather than by a
method taken on trust. Both transcriptions were then compared byte for byte
against the `d` attribute they came from.

The 2026-08-30 fetch did the same thing twice over. It re-ran the command
against `anthropic.svg` and got `1cc599f6…` again, and it recomputed every
contrast number in the table above from the hexes rather than copying the ones
already written down — reproducing 14.83, 1.02, 17.58, 17.71, 1.22, 21.00, 3.32,
4.37, 3.93, 2.16, 6.71 and 2.56 exactly. A method that reproduces two
independent sets of already-accepted numbers is the only reason the new rows
beside them are worth anything.

The correction made later the same day was held to that standard before a word
of it was written, because the sentence it replaced was wrong precisely for
having skipped it. All five `-color.svg` URLs were requested one at a time and
their status recorded as returned — 404 for `groq-color.svg` and
`baseten-color.svg`, 200 for `together-color.svg`, `cerebras-color.svg` and
`fireworks-color.svg` — and `openai-color.svg` and `xai-color.svg` were
requested too, and answered 404. The monochrome file beside each of the five was
fetched again and reproduced the checksum already on its line above. Every
colour file's `d` attributes were compared byte for byte against the constants
in `ProviderMark.kt` by a program rather than by eye, since a fill that is not
on the transcribed path is a fill for a different drawing. The contrast routine
was re-run over the whole existing table and reproduced every number already
written in it before it was trusted with the five new hexes. And
`data/simple-icons.json` was re-read at the pinned version in the same pass:
3453 icons, every hex this file attributes to that distributor unchanged, and no
icon under the title OpenAI or xAI, which is what makes the third class above a
statement about that file rather than about a memory of it.
